note: Every change made because it was claimed to shorten the ETA. judge_on is set when the change lands, not when it is convenient. concurrent_changes is what else was in flight, so a later reader can tell a clean attribution from a confounded one.

predictions.claim: Replacing the 0.5% guessed reservation with a bound derived from real consumption frees discretionary budget, so more laps fit in the same week.
predictions.metric: discretionary_percent reported by scripts/pacing.mjs, and laps per day in state/laps.json

predictions.claim: The registry listed revenue-loop as enabled after the owner stopped it, so the gate reserved quota for a trigger that cannot fire. Marking it disabled returns that share.
Ranking efficiency last while every path is infinite stops the loop spending laps on acceleration, so the next laps pick a candidate that could make a path finite.
predictions.metric: the kind of candidate chosen by each lap, read from state/continue.json and commit subjects

predictions.claim: Every candidate was a build act and none was a distribution act, while all three outside refutations landed on distribution. Adding findable_surface_at_scale and stopping discredited estimates from outranking honest blanks should change which candidate a lap actually executes.
predictions.metric: state/continue.json / state/laps.json show the next lap that selects work choosing a distribution-class candidate (findable_surface_at_scale, or the itch page judged on being found and referred) rather than a fifth build candidate. Falsified if laps keep selecting build candidates or machinery while the reranking sits unread.
concurrent_changes: codex INBOX task 2026-08-09.h aims the outside survey at the new candidate, so a refutation may arrive before the judge date and settle it the other way
predictions.note: The candidate deliberately carries no days-to-first-yen. Judging this on a day count would reproduce the exact error the change corrects, so it is judged on what gets executed.
